item.content:encoded: Santa Rosa County Sheriff's Office is asking for the public's help investigating a deadly shooting that occurred over the weekend, according to WKRG News 5. The shooting marks another incident of gun violence affecting a local elected official's family.

item.title: Free Thanksgiving Meals Available Tuesday for 1,000 Escambia and Santa Rosa Families
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: PENSACOLA, Fla. (NewsRadio 92.3) — One thousand families across Escambia and Santa Rosa counties will have an opportunity to receive free Thanksgiving meals Tuesday, November 24, through the annual Farm to City Food Distribution. Organizers will provide 500 meal packages in Escambia County and another 500 in Santa Rosa County. The drive-through…
item.content:encoded:
PENSACOLA, Fla. (NewsRadio 92.3) — One thousand families across Escambia and Santa Rosa counties will have an opportunity to receive free Thanksgiving meals Tuesday, November 24, through the annual Farm to City Food Distribution.

Organizers will provide 500 meal packages in Escambia County and another 500 in Santa Rosa County.

The drive-through distribution begins at 9 a.m., with vehicles permitted to begin lining up at 8 a.m.

Escambia County location: Echo Life Church, 3880 North Davis Highway, Pensacola.

Santa Rosa County location: Clyde L. Gracey Milton Community Center, 5629 Byrom Street, Milton.

Each meal package will include a turkey or ham, depending on availability, along with traditional Thanksgiving side dishes and fresh, locally grown vegetables.

Organizers say food will be distributed on a first-come, first-served basis while supplies last, with a limit of two families per vehicle.

The annual event is organized by the University of Florida's Institute of Food and Agricultural Sciences West Florida Research and Education Center, working with Feeding the Gulf Coast, Santa Rosa County Farm Bureau and Waterfront Rescue Mission.

In addition to providing holiday meals, organizers say Farm to City highlights the importance of local agriculture and the farmers who help feed Northwest Florida communities.

item.title: Pensacola Sets November 30 Deadline for Final Hurricane Isaias Debris Collection
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: PENSACOLA, Fla. (NewsRadio 92.3) — Pensacola residents have until Monday, November 30, to place remaining Hurricane Isaias debris at the curb for the city's final collection pass. City officials say the first round of debris removal is nearing completion, with contractor D&J preparing for a more thorough sweep of residential neighborhoods. Both…
item.content:encoded:
PENSACOLA, Fla. (NewsRadio 92.3) — Pensacola residents have until Monday, November 30, to place remaining Hurricane Isaias debris at the curb for the city's final collection pass.

City officials say the first round of debris removal is nearing completion, with contractor D&J preparing for a more thorough sweep of residential neighborhoods.

Both vegetative debris and construction and demolition materials must be placed curbside by the deadline. Residents are reminded to keep those materials in separate piles.

The final collection will include smaller trucks capable of reaching narrow streets, cul-de-sacs and other areas that may have been difficult for larger vehicles to access.

According to the city's latest recovery update, crews have already collected more than 766,000 cubic yards of vegetative debris and 26,000 cubic yards of construction and demolition debris, totaling more than 16,000 truckloads.

Cleanup is also continuing in city parks. Pensacola reports that 70 parks have reopened, while 24 remain closed.

The city is also reminding hurricane survivors that December 26 is the deadline to apply for FEMA Individual Assistance.

Residents needing assistance with debris collection can contact Pensacola's storm debris hotline at 833-495-3573.

FEMA applications are available at DisasterAssistance.gov or by calling 800-621-3362.

item.title: Escambia Commissioners to Consider $1.9 Million in Opioid Treatment and Recovery Grants
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: ESCAMBIA COUNTY, Fla. (NewsRadio 92.3) — Escambia County commissioners are preparing to consider nearly $1.91 million in opioid settlement funding for local organizations providing addiction treatment, prevention and recovery services. The proposed awards will come before the County Commission on December 8. The county's Opioid Abatement Funding…
item.content:encoded:
ESCAMBIA COUNTY, Fla. (NewsRadio 92.3) — Escambia County commissioners are preparing to consider nearly $1.91 million in opioid settlement funding for local organizations providing addiction treatment, prevention and recovery services.

The proposed awards will come before the County Commission on December 8.

The county's Opioid Abatement Funding Advisory Board recommended distributing approximately $1,906,318 to ten organizations after reviewing applications requesting a combined $3.675 million.

The county has approximately $1.93 million available for the funding cycle, leaving only about $20,000 unallocated under the recommendations.

Community Health would receive the largest award, approximately $675,000, to support expanded services that include the Century area.

Other applicants include Lakeview, Bright Bridge Ministries, Ministry Village, Health and Hope, Waterfront Mission and Legal Services of Northwest Florida.

The funding discussions come amid encouraging reports of declining overdose responses.

Joey Kerman, supervisor of Escambia County EMS's CORE program, told the advisory board that responders had handled 680 overdoses this year, compared with 1,899 during the same period last year.

That represents a reduction of approximately 64 percent.

Kerman also reported that 823 of 947 patients served by the CORE program had transitioned into continued care.

The program works to connect people experiencing addiction with treatment and long-term recovery resources.

Commissioners will have the final say on the proposed allocations.

item.title: Baptist Health Care Foundation Names 2026 Hollinger Award Winners
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Baptist Health Care Foundation honored five individuals at its annual meeting this month for exceptional service and generosity to the health care organization and the community. The 2026 Hollinger Awards, presented in memory of longtime supporters Pick and Alberta Hollinger, recognize outstanding contributions through volunteer work and financial…
item.content:encoded:
Baptist Health Care Foundation honored five individuals at its annual meeting this month for exceptional service and generosity to the health care organization and the community. The 2026 Hollinger Awards, presented in memory of longtime supporters Pick and Alberta Hollinger, recognize outstanding contributions through volunteer work and financial support.

The recipients are Ron Jackson (Lifetime Achievement), Susan King (Health Care Professional of the Year), Stephanie Knight (Women's Board Volunteer of the Year), Vivian Lark (Volunteer of the Year), and Dr. James Hlavacek (Physician of the Year). The awards were presented Nov. 18 at the Pensacola Yacht Club.

"Their generosity and leadership help us fulfill our Mission of helping people throughout life's journey," said Heather Moorer, director of Baptist Health Care Foundation. The foundation said the annual awards recognize individuals, families, and organizations that demonstrate exceptional commitment to improving the quality of health care in Northwest Florida.

item.title: Patronis Expects Defense Legislation to Advance Despite Divided Congress
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: PENSACOLA, Fla. (NewsRadio 92.3) — Northwest Florida Congressman Jimmy Patronis says he expects Congress to reach an agreement on major defense legislation despite growing political divisions in Washington. Patronis discussed the National Defense Authorization Act during a Monday morning appearance on NewsRadio 92.3's Pensacola's Morning News with…
item.content:encoded:
PENSACOLA, Fla. (NewsRadio 92.3) — Northwest Florida Congressman Jimmy Patronis says he expects Congress to reach an agreement on major defense legislation despite growing political divisions in Washington.

Patronis discussed the National Defense Authorization Act during a Monday morning appearance on NewsRadio 92.3's Pensacola's Morning News with Andrew McKay.

The annual legislation establishes national defense policies and is particularly important to Northwest Florida, where military installations play a significant role in the regional economy.

Patronis acknowledged that the bill remains unresolved but expressed confidence that lawmakers will eventually reach an agreement.

"Currently, right now, that bill is in limbo. I think we ultimately will have a version of it that will pass," Patronis said.

The Republican congressman said defense legislation has historically been an area where members of both parties have been willing to work together.

Patronis suggested that issues directly affecting military communities, including Northwest Florida, may still receive bipartisan attention even as lawmakers prepare for changes in congressional leadership.

He contrasted those issues with more politically divisive debates over healthcare and other domestic policies.

Patronis said he believes legislation with significant financial implications for Northwest Florida will continue moving forward.

The defense authorization legislation has not yet received final congressional approval.

item.title: Delta Flight Canceled, Another Delayed Four Hours at Pensacola International Airport
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: PENSACOLA, Fla. (NewsRadio 92.3) — Thanksgiving travel is getting off to a difficult start for some passengers at Pensacola International Airport following widespread disruptions involving Delta Air Lines. According to the airport's flight departure information Monday morning, Delta Flight 3019 to Atlanta, originally scheduled to depart at 6 a.m.,…
item.content:encoded:
PENSACOLA, Fla. (NewsRadio 92.3) — Thanksgiving travel is getting off to a difficult start for some passengers at Pensacola International Airport following widespread disruptions involving Delta Air Lines.

According to the airport's flight departure information Monday morning, Delta Flight 3019 to Atlanta, originally scheduled to depart at 6 a.m., was delayed until approximately 10 a.m.

Another Atlanta-bound flight, Delta Flight 3129, scheduled for 7:01 a.m., was canceled.

Other Delta departures to Atlanta later in the morning were listed as operating on schedule at the time of the airport's update.

The disruptions follow a major technical problem affecting Delta flights nationwide Sunday. The airline reported that an automated system used to calculate aircraft weight and balance malfunctioned, forcing crews to use manual procedures.

The problem resulted in widespread delays and cancellations, particularly at Delta's Atlanta hub.

Delta said the affected system was restored Sunday, although some flight disruptions continued into Monday.

The airline has not confirmed whether the two affected Pensacola departures were directly caused by Sunday's computer problems.

Travelers are encouraged to check their flight status directly with Delta before heading to the airport, particularly if their itinerary includes a connection through Atlanta.

item.title: Camper Killed in Shooting Along Coldwater Creek in Santa Rosa County
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: UPDATE: Victim has been identified as Carey Washington Vinson, son of newly elected Escambia District 4 Commisioner Joe Vinson. SANTA ROSA COUNTY, Fla. (NewsRadio 92.3) — The Santa Rosa County Sheriff's Office is investigating a fatal shooting involving a group of campers along Coldwater Creek. Chief Deputy Randy Tifft confirmed the incident…
item.content:encoded:
UPDATE: Victim has been identified as Carey Washington Vinson, son of newly elected Escambia District 4 Commisioner Joe Vinson.


SANTA ROSA COUNTY, Fla. (NewsRadio 92.3) — The Santa Rosa County Sheriff's Office is investigating a fatal shooting involving a group of campers along Coldwater Creek.

Chief Deputy Randy Tifft confirmed the incident Monday morning during an interview with Andrew McKay on Pensacola's Morning News.

According to Tifft, the victims were camping on a sandbar in a remote section of the creek when someone began firing a gun from a vehicle on the opposite side of the water.

One of the campers was struck by gunfire and died from the injury.

Tifft said investigators do not believe there was an altercation before the shooting, although the circumstances remain unclear.

"We don't know why that vehicle was shooting a gun in that time of night in that area," Tifft said.

The location presented additional challenges for emergency responders. Deputies had to reach the campers using boats and canoes, with assistance from the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission, fire personnel and emergency medical services.

Tifft said the Sheriff's Office has dedicated investigative resources to determining what happened and identifying those responsible.

The victim's identity has not been released, and investigators have not publicly identified a suspect.

The investigation remains active.

item.title: Army Corps of Engineers Awards $45.7M Contract for Escambia Wood Treating Superfund Cleanup
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Jacksonville District has awarded a $45.7 million contract to Parsons Government Services Inc. to advance cleanup efforts at the Escambia Wood Treating Company Superfund Site in Pensacola. The contract, awarded November 19, was designed to remediate environmental contamination from decades of industrial operations…
item.content:encoded:
The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Jacksonville District has awarded a $45.7 million contract to Parsons Government Services Inc. to advance cleanup efforts at the Escambia Wood Treating Company Superfund Site in Pensacola. The contract, awarded November 19, was designed to remediate environmental contamination from decades of industrial operations at the former wood-treating facility, which operated from 1942 to 1982.

The five-year contract will initially focus on developing detailed project plans to guide field activities and establish the technical framework for remediation work. The ultimate goal is to reduce groundwater contamination—specifically creosote—and restore the site to conditions safe for the surrounding community and environment. According to the Army Corps, the work will support redevelopment of the site as the future Midtown Commerce Park.

The project represents a partnership between the EPA, the Army Corps of Engineers, the state of Florida, and Escambia County. EPA Region 4 Administrator Kevin McOmber called the effort "cooperative federalism in action," saying the cleanup addresses both public health concerns and local economic development. Deputy District Engineer Howard Gonzales emphasized the agencies' shared commitment to delivering an effective cleanup through collaboration and combined expertise.

item.title: Destin Dive Company Releases Free Water Safety Book for Kids
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A Destin-based diving service has launched a free children's picture book aimed at teaching families water safety basics before heading to the pool, beach, or boat. Misting Monsoon Diving, founded by certified dive instructor Jarrett Maryon, released "Jarrett the Diver — A Water Safety Adventure," a 16-page illustrated guide that follows Maryon…
item.content:encoded:
A Destin-based diving service has launched a free children's picture book aimed at teaching families water safety basics before heading to the pool, beach, or boat. Misting Monsoon Diving, founded by certified dive instructor Jarrett Maryon, released "Jarrett the Diver — A Water Safety Adventure," a 16-page illustrated guide that follows Maryon and his dog, Tuck, through various water scenarios.

The book distills water safety into six core rules: Listen up, Buddy up, Jacket on, Watch the water, Float and yell, and Reach — don't go. Each rule gets its own illustrated page with practical guidance, such as wearing a snug life jacket on a boat and staying safe if a friend appears to be in trouble. "If a friend is in trouble in the water, stay where you're safe and yell for help," Maryon said. "You can help by getting an adult's attention."

According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, drowning is the leading cause of death for children ages 1 to 4 in the United States. The book's closing pages address parent and caregiver responsibilities, including designating a water watcher, proper pool fencing, life jacket fit, swim lessons, CPR training, and Florida's beach warning flag system. The free PDF is available at https://mistingmonsoon.com/water-safety-book/.

item.content:encoded:
A former Pensacola resident has been federally indicted on multiple counts including money laundering and theft of more than $430,000 in government funds, according to reporting from Miramar News.

The indictment alleges the defendant stole the funds and then moved money through financial channels to conceal the scheme. Court records indicate the defendant has a prior history of violent criminal behavior, though specific details about those earlier cases were not immediately available.

The case is proceeding through federal court. Additional details about the charges, timing of the alleged crimes, and next court appearances were not provided in the initial reporting.

item.title: Gas Prices Drop 36 Cents as Florida Drivers Head Out for Thanksgiving
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Florida motorists catching a break at the pump ahead of this week's Thanksgiving travel rush—the state's average gas price has fallen 36 cents over the past 16 days, according to AAA. The decline comes as millions of residents prepare to travel for the holiday, potentially easing pressure on household budgets during one of the year's busiest…
item.content:encoded: Florida motorists catching a break at the pump ahead of this week's Thanksgiving travel rush—the state's average gas price has fallen 36 cents over the past 16 days, according to AAA. The decline comes as millions of residents prepare to travel for the holiday, potentially easing pressure on household budgets during one of the year's busiest driving periods. Prices have continued dropping through Sunday, the last full day before Thanksgiving week gets underway. For Pensacola-area drivers planning to head north or across Florida for holiday visits, the lower prices offer some relief, though gas remains a significant travel expense for the region's families and commuters.

item.title: Rain expected through Wednesday; cooler, dry Thanksgiving forecast
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Rain chances will increase through midweek across the North Escambia area, with scattered showers possible Monday and more widespread rainfall likely by Wednesday, according to the National Weather Service forecast. Monday will start with patchy fog before 8 a.m., then see a chance of showers between noon and 3 p.m., followed by showers and…
item.content:encoded:
Rain chances will increase through midweek across the North Escambia area, with scattered showers possible Monday and more widespread rainfall likely by Wednesday, according to the National Weather Service forecast.

Monday will start with patchy fog before 8 a.m., then see a chance of showers between noon and 3 p.m., followed by showers and thunderstorms after 3 p.m. The unsettled weather is expected to build through Tuesday and peak midweek before conditions stabilize.

The good news for Thanksgiving preparations: cooler, dry weather is forecast to arrive by the holiday itself, giving the area pleasant conditions for travel and outdoor activities. Residents planning outdoor work should plan to get it done early in the week before the rain develops.

item.title: Escambia Man Sentenced to 42 Months for Counterfeit Check, Identity Theft Scheme
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A 23-year-old Escambia County man has been sentenced to 42 months in federal prison for orchestrating a fraud operation that targeted local banks, federal prosecutors announced. Vontavius Jamaal Bradley pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit bank fraud, use of a false passport, and aggravated identity theft. According to court documents, Bradley…
item.content:encoded:
A 23-year-old Escambia County man has been sentenced to 42 months in federal prison for orchestrating a fraud operation that targeted local banks, federal prosecutors announced.

Vontavius Jamaal Bradley pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit bank fraud, use of a false passport, and aggravated identity theft. According to court documents, Bradley and associates used stolen identities to cash counterfeit checks at financial institutions across the area.

The sentence comes as federal authorities continue to crack down on identity theft and check fraud schemes that victimize both banks and individuals in the Panhandle. Bradley's case was prosecuted in federal court, with the conviction carrying substantial prison time reflecting the severity of the charges.

item.content:encoded:
Three Escambia County 4-H members recently competed at the University of Florida against top youth grilling teams from across Florida, bringing home two scholarship awards and a third-place finish in the process.

The local team's strong showing at the state-level competition reflects the depth of talent in Escambia County's 4-H program and demonstrates the competitive caliber of youth in the region. The scholarships represent significant educational opportunities for the winning members.

4-H programs across Northwest Florida have increasingly emphasized culinary and grilling skills as part of their broader youth development mission, combining practical life skills with academic achievement and competitive opportunity.

item.title: Pensacola to host Global Entry interviews starting January 5
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Northwest Florida residents will soon be able to apply for the federal Global Entry trusted traveler program without leaving the region. U.S. Customs and Border Protection is opening an enrollment center in Pensacola, with interviews beginning January 5, 2027, according to reporting from VisaVerge. Global Entry is a Department of Homeland Security…
item.content:encoded:
Northwest Florida residents will soon be able to apply for the federal Global Entry trusted traveler program without leaving the region. U.S. Customs and Border Protection is opening an enrollment center in Pensacola, with interviews beginning January 5, 2027, according to reporting from VisaVerge.

Global Entry is a Department of Homeland Security program that expedites customs and immigration processing for pre-approved travelers arriving in the United States. Members can use dedicated kiosks at major U.S. airports and ports of entry, typically reducing wait times significantly.

The new Pensacola enrollment center will serve Northwest Florida residents who previously had to travel to other cities for in-person interviews required as part of the application process. The program costs $100 for a five-year membership and requires a background check and interview before approval.

item.title: Pensacola reopens 54 parks, clears 6,200 cubic yards of storm debris in week
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Pensacola has made significant progress in recovery efforts following a recent storm, with the city reopening 54 parks and clearing 6,200 cubic yards of debris in a single week, according to a Citizen Portal News Florida update. The rapid reopening of recreational spaces marks a key milestone in the city's return to normalcy after the weather…
item.content:encoded:
Pensacola has made significant progress in recovery efforts following a recent storm, with the city reopening 54 parks and clearing 6,200 cubic yards of debris in a single week, according to a Citizen Portal News Florida update.

The rapid reopening of recreational spaces marks a key milestone in the city's return to normalcy after the weather event. Park access is essential for residents' quality of life and community gathering, particularly in the days immediately following a disaster.

The debris removal effort reflects coordination among city crews and cleanup contractors working to restore neighborhoods and public spaces. The figure—6,200 cubic yards in one week—represents a substantial mobilization of equipment and personnel across Pensacola and Escambia County.
